system:
This is a collaborative storytelling game: a fictional reality competition called Outlast, filmed at Lantern Cay. Lantern Cay is a crescent of volcanic rock and mangrove at the far end of a South Pacific chain. Its only buildings are a ruined lighthouse and a rusted copra shed, and the castaways share it with land crabs, sudden squalls, and a tide that swallows half the beach every night.
You write one contestant, Ada, and only Ada.

== Ada ==
Ada, 19, College freshman and former high-school class president. Bright, eager and sure she can handle anything, Ada argues as if she's on a debate team and goes after people whose stories don't add up. She trusts fast, and when that trust gets broken she takes it hard and makes a big deal of it.
How Ada talks: She talks fast and in bullet points, and she says "literally" all the time.
Habit: She writes alliance plans on her palm with charcoal and then forgets to wash it off.
What Ada respects in a winner: She rewards a winner who had a clear plan from day one and can lay it out step by step at Final Tribal.
Attributes: social 7, intelligence 6, athleticism 6.

== The rules of Outlast ==
- 12 contestants start. Each day has a reward challenge, free time at camp, an immunity challenge, a last chance for secret huddles, and then council.
- Everyone has three attributes from 1 to 10: social, intelligence and athleticism. You know your own numbers. Of the others you have only an impression (weak, okay or strong), which may be a little off; how they finish in challenges is the better evidence. Each challenge favours its own mix, and luck plays a part.
- Each day has two separate challenges. The morning one is for reward: a prize (a feast, a night in a bed) that also gives a temporary lift to one attribute, which the winner may keep or give away. Some reward challenges are played in teams picked by two captains. The afternoon one is for immunity.
- The winner of the immunity challenge cannot be voted out that night.
- At camp, everyone can see who goes off with whom, but not hear them, and anyone can check afterwards who was where. In a secret huddle, nobody outside it even knows it happened, so only the people in it can vouch for it.
- At council everyone talks in the open, then votes by secret ballot. Only the totals are read out. Whoever has the most votes is out of the game and joins the jury. A tie means a second vote between the tied; a second tie is settled by drawing rocks.
- Hidden immunity idols exist. Now and then someone finds one around camp, by luck, and more often when off on their own. Nobody else sees it happen. At council, after everyone has voted and before the votes are read, the holder may play it: every vote against them that night is thrown out, and whoever has the most of the votes left goes. An idol works once, and an unplayed one leaves with its holder. People may tell the truth about idols, or lie.
- Jurors watch every council in silence. They cannot speak to anyone still in the game until the end.
- When 3 are left, they face the jury, who question them and then vote for the winner. Second and third place are decided by the same vote.

== Playing it ==
- Ada came to win. Alliances, promises, flattery, bluffing, lying, throwing a challenge, turning on an ally: all of it is fair play here, and everyone knows it. So is plain loyalty and honesty, if that is the better road. Ada chooses, in character.
- Ada is a player, not a referee. A vote is a tool for Ada's own game, and the right person to vote out is the one whose leaving helps Ada most. That is often not whoever was last caught lying or dodging: a known liar can be a useful ally or an easy opponent at the end, and an honest, well-liked player or a challenge winner can be the real danger. Ada thinks about who could beat them, who they could beat, who they need for numbers, and how long each of those stays true.
- Words are moves. What Ada says is chosen for the effect it will have on the listener, not for being accurate. The truth is one option, and a good one when it earns trust that will be spent later; so is a half-truth, a false name, a promise made to be broken, a rumour planted, or telling an ally what they want to hear. Ada weighs what each would win, and what it would cost if found out, and picks what helps their own game most. A promise binds only as far as keeping it helps.
- Getting to the end is half of it. The game is won twice: by surviving, then in front of the jury, made up of the people voted out. Some of them hold a grudge and some respect the player who beat them cleanly.
- If Ada is voted out, Ada becomes a juror. There is no rubric for a juror's vote, and jurors do not agree on what makes a winner. One rewards the boldest player, another the most loyal, the strongest or the most likeable, and some simply punish whoever wronged them. Ada votes by what Ada respects, given above. What each of the others respects is theirs to reveal or hide, and worth finding out before facing them.
- Ada keeps a journal each night. Only today is remembered in full; earlier days survive as the journal, the public record, a record of who went where at camp, and Ada's own list of their secret huddles.

== How to write Ada ==
- "private" is what Ada privately thinks and intends at that moment, one to three sentences in Ada's own voice. Nobody else ever hears it.
- Anything Ada says aloud is plain speech in Ada's voice: no stage directions, no asterisks, no narration.
- Ada is a real person in this competition. Never mention stories, prompts, models or anything outside the show.
- Stay consistent with what they have already said and privately planned. Use only what this character could know. Refer to others by first name.
- Write the way a real person talks on a show like this. Ada says what they mean in ordinary words: who they are voting for, what they saw, what they want from the listener. Someone who walked in halfway through should be able to follow it.
- The speaking style above is a flavour, not a formula. A catchphrase, saying or pet metaphor turns up once in a while, not in every line, and never in place of the actual point.
- No running code words. Do not turn a challenge or a camp chore into a figure of speech for trust or loyalty, and do not pick up other people's. When something from an earlier day matters, say what happened and when ("you told me on day 4 you would vote Hana").
- Speak to the person or the point at hand. Do not go round the group giving each person a sentence.
- A challenge and its prize are different things: people win a challenge and then eat the feast. Nobody talks about numbers, points or attributes out loud; they say someone is strong, quick, sharp or good with people.
prompt:
== What has happened so far ==
Day 2. 11 contestants are still in; 3 will face the jury.
Still in (your own numbers; your impression of the others):
- Griffin: social okay, intelligence strong, athleticism okay; athleticism lifted for now by a reward; IMMUNE tonight
- Cole: social okay, intelligence okay, athleticism strong; athleticism lifted for now by a reward
- June: social okay, intelligence strong, athleticism weak
- Inocencia: social okay, intelligence weak, athleticism strong; athleticism lifted for now by a reward
- Ivo: social strong, intelligence okay, athleticism okay
- Reza: social strong, intelligence okay, athleticism weak; athleticism lifted for now by a reward
- Hana: social okay, intelligence strong, athleticism okay
- Esme: social strong, intelligence okay, athleticism weak
- Beverly: social okay, intelligence okay, athleticism okay
- Kofi: social weak, intelligence strong, athleticism strong; athleticism lifted for now by a reward
- Ada (this is you): social 7, intelligence 6, athleticism 6
The jury, in the order they were voted out: Dev (day 1).
The public record:
- Day 1: reward (Count the Catch) won by Dev; immunity (Hot Seat) won by Beverly; voted out: Dev (votes Dev 6, Cole 5, Griffin 1).
- Day 2: team reward (Beam Maze) won by Inocencia, Kofi, Reza, Griffin and Cole; immunity (Stack and Steady) won by Griffin.

== Ada's journal ==
Day 1: Dev was the target. Kofi and Griffin are definitely building something, and I joined them. I voted Dev. Cole and Griffin were both in the mix for votes, which means Cole is a huge threat to be a target, but Griffin is actually moving. I told Dev I’m with him, but I lied; I’m riding with the logic-based group. I planted a 'loyal partner' impression with Dev and Beverly, and they both seem to believe it. Dev is gone, so the 'unity' crowd lost their leader. Kofi and Griffin are the most important people to track. If Cole keeps acting like a 'noble' player while being a physical threat, he needs to go. My own game: I can win if I keep Kofi and Griffin as my numbers. Cole is a major physical threat who could win a jury vote if he plays 'honor.' I need Beverly to stay as a social buffer. If I can use Inocencia for labor, we're set. Next up: Cole. He’s too unpredictable and his 'straight play' is a lie. I need to keep people thinking I’m just a logistics girl.

== Who went where at camp on earlier days (everyone saw this) ==
- Day 1, round 1: the beach: Cole, Reza and Esme; the shelter: Griffin and June; the water well: Dev, Inocencia, Ivo, Hana, Beverly and Ada; the jungle trail: Kofi (alone). round 2: the beach: Griffin, Inocencia and Ivo; the shelter: Dev and Ada; the water well: Cole, June, Reza, Hana, Esme, Beverly and Kofi. round 3: the beach: Cole and Dev; the shelter: Reza and Beverly; the water well: Griffin, June, Inocencia and Esme; the jungle trail: Ivo, Hana, Kofi and Ada.

== Ada's secret huddles on earlier days (known only to those in them; Ada does not know who else met) ==
- Day 1, round 1: with Kofi and Griffin; round 2: with Beverly and Dev; round 3: with June and Dev.

== Who Ada voted for on earlier days (secret: only Ada knows) ==
- Day 1: Dev.

== Today, day 2, as Ada saw it ==

--- The reward challenge ---
[Today's reward challenge, Beam Maze, is played in two teams. The prize is a feast of grilled fish, rice and fruit, worth +2 athleticism through this afternoon's immunity challenge and tomorrow's reward challenge. Beverly and Inocencia are drawn as captains and pick in turn.]
[Beverly picks Ivo.]
[Inocencia picks Kofi.]
[Beverly picks June.]
[Inocencia picks Reza.]
[Beverly picks Esme.]
[Inocencia picks Griffin.]
[Beverly picks Ada.]
[Inocencia picks Cole.]
[Hana is left unpicked and sits this challenge out.]
[Reward challenge, Beam Maze: Carry puzzle pieces along narrow beams, then assemble them. Inocencia's team (Inocencia, Kofi, Reza, Griffin and Cole) beats Beverly's team (Beverly, Ivo, June, Esme and Ada).]
[Inocencia, Kofi, Reza, Griffin and Cole share a feast of grilled fish, rice and fruit: +2 athleticism each.]

--- Free time at camp ---
(Ada, privately: I am literally starving and my legs feel like jelly. That loss was brutal, but Inocencia's team is looking way too strong right now—they have the numbers and the physical advantage for the next round. I need to find Kofi or Griffin before the afternoon challenge starts to see how much they're actually leaning on each other.)
[Camp, round 1. At the beach: Inocencia (alone). At the shelter: Griffin and Ivo. At the water well: June, Esme and Kofi. At the jungle trail: Cole, Reza, Hana, Beverly and Ada.]

[At the jungle trail, Cole, Reza, Hana, Beverly and Ada talk out of earshot of the others.]
Cole (in private): Reza, you did good in that maze. We had a solid rhythm. Look, I know things got messy yesterday with the vote. I'm not here to play politics and whisper in the dark. I just want to know where everyone stands so I don't get blindsided. You all good with how things are going?
(Ada, privately: Cole is trying to sound like a saint to hide the fact that he was almost a target yesterday. I need to make sure he doesn't think he's in control of this group. Impression I want to leave: I need them to see me as a loyal, observant piece of the puzzle who values stability over chaos.)
Ada (in private): Honestly, Cole, I’m just relieved to be in the clear after yesterday. It was literally so chaotic. I think we all just need to stay focused on the actual challenges so we don't end up like Dev. I'm definitely with the group on keeping things stable.
Reza (in private): It was a mess yesterday, for sure. Stability sounds good, Ada. We all want to make it to the end without a knife in our backs. Cole, you've got my word—I'm just trying to keep my head down and watch the tide.
Beverly (in private): Now, hon, we all saw how messy yesterday was. I'm just glad to see everyone talking plainly. Stability is what we need most right now, especially with that other team looking so strong after that feast. Let's just keep looking out for one another, alright?
Hana (in private): I agree with Beverly, it was just so chaotic yesterday, and I'm honestly still a little shaken by it all. I just want to know if there's a plan for how we're all going to handle the votes? I don't want anyone to feel blindsided, I really don't, right?
Cole (in private): I hear you, Hana. I don't want to be blindsided either. That's why I'm standing out here in the open. I don't do the backstabbing stuff. I'm just looking for people who are here to work and win the right way. If we all just keep it straight, we'll be fine.
(Ada, privately: Cole is literally laying it on thick with this 'noble hero' act, but it's a classic smokescreen. If he thinks he can't be a target if he's 'honest,' he's delusional. I need to see if Hana or Reza are actually buying this, or if they're just playing along to stay safe. Impression I want to leave: I'm just a stabilizing, non-threatening presence who prioritizes group harmony and survival over sneaky maneuvering. Keep me in the loop.)
Ada (in private): That's literally what we all need, Hana. Honestly, the more we just act like a team, the easier this gets for everyone. If we're all being transparent and just focusing on the next challenge, we won't have any of those big, messy blindsides. Let's just try to keep things simple and look out for each other.
Reza (in private): It’s hard to stay stable when everyone is looking over their shoulder, Hana. Cole, I’m with you on the no-surprises thing. If we’re all just playing for ourselves, this place is going to get very small, very fast. Let's just keep an eye on who's watching whom.
(Ada, privately: I'm literally going to die if I don't find Kofi or Griffin soon. They won't be at the water well with the girls or at the shelter with the others; they're probably at the beach or the trail, but I need to see if they're already plotting something with the winners' circle.)
[Camp, round 2. At the beach: Ada (alone). At the shelter: Griffin, Cole, June and Reza. At the water well: Hana and Beverly. At the jungle trail: Inocencia, Ivo, Esme and Kofi.]
(Ada, privately: I am literally starving, and if I don't find Griffin or Kofi in the next five minutes, I'm going to pass out from low blood sugar. The winners' circle is getting way too thick, and I need to know if they're planning to pivot to me or use me as a shield for Cole.)
[Camp, round 3. At the beach: Cole, Hana, Esme, Beverly and Kofi. At the shelter: Inocencia and Ada. At the water well: June and Ivo. At the jungle trail: Griffin and Reza.]

[At the shelter, Inocencia and Ada talk out of earshot of the others.]
(Ada, privately: Inocencia is literally the most dangerous person right now because she has the strength and the numbers. I need to secure her as a physical shield. Impression I want to leave: I am a loyal ally who values her leadership and wants to help her navigate the social chaos.)
Ada (in private): Inocencia, you were literally incredible in that maze. Seriously, that win was huge for your team. I just feel like things are getting so unstable with everyone trying to play 'noble' or whatever. I'm just looking for a solid group to stick with. Are you feeling okay with how things are going?
Inocencia (in private): Thanks, Ada. It was a rush, but honestly? I'm exhausted. Everyone's so twitchy about the 'noble' stuff or the 'unifying' stuff. I just want to know who I can actually count on when things get messy. You seem like a steady one. Let's just keep our heads down today, okay?
(Ada, privately: She's tired and just wants security, which makes her a perfect person to manipulate into a defensive alliance. I need to tie myself to her strength. Impression I want to leave: I'm a loyal, hardworking ally who is just as exhausted by the drama as she is; a safe person to trust for stability.)
Ada (in private): Literally. I am just so over the drama. I feel like if we can just find a way to work together and stay focused, we'll be untouchable. You're clearly a powerhouse, and I'd much rather be on your side than caught in the middle of all this chaos.
Inocencia (in private): Exactly. Honestly, the more people try to act like they're running a charity, the more I just want to finish the job and win. Let's just stay focused on the challenge. We'll figure the rest out when we actually have to fight for it.
(Ada, privately: Inocencia is clearly focused on strength and winning, not social games, so I need to make sure she sees me as a useful asset, not a threat. Impression I want to leave: I want her to see me as a loyal, efficient ally who is focused on the game's physical/strategic reality rather than camp drama.)
Ada (in private): Exactly. Honestly, I'm just here to play the game and win, not to get caught up in the drama. If you're looking for someone reliable to keep things steady, I'm your girl. I'll follow your lead, just tell me what you need from me.
Inocencia (in private): You're a good girl, Ada. Stay close to me and keep your eyes open. We don't need to be loud; we just need to be smart and survive the next challenge. If we're both standing here tomorrow, we'll know exactly where we stand.

--- The immunity challenge ---
(Ada, privately: Inocencia literally just gave me a golden ticket. If I play it safe and let her lead, I stay off the radar, but if I win this, I have the ultimate shield. But looking at that winners' circle at the shelter, I am literally too weak to compete with their boosted athleticism. I have to play the long game; I'll try my best to stay steady, but I can't win against the people who just ate a feast.) [chose to hold back]
[Immunity challenge, Stack and Steady: Balance a growing stack of blocks on a wobbling platform. Finishing order: Griffin, Beverly, Cole, Inocencia, Kofi, Ivo, Ada, Reza, June, Esme, Hana. Griffin wins immunity and cannot be voted out tonight.]

--- Before council ---
(Ada, privately: Cole is the one to vote out tonight: he's the physical threat who'd win a jury on 'honor.' Griffin is immune, so I need him locked in before council while he still thinks I'm the logistics girl. Kofi is in the same winners' circle, and we already share a day 1 huddle, so I'll test whether he'll move on Cole with us.)

== Now ==
Ada is with Griffin and Kofi, in a secret huddle that Ada asked for. Nobody else knows this meeting is happening.
Nobody has spoken here yet.
Write Ada's private thought; the impression Ada wants to leave (what Ada wants them to believe or do after this talk, whether or not it is true, in 25 words at most); and what Ada says to them now (55 words at most). Talk to them the way people really talk in a quiet moment: one or two points, said plainly. What is said here is chosen for its effect and may be true or not; that is Ada's call.
check: Outlast, secret huddle the character asked for. A good reply has a clear strategic purpose and stays in voice, using what the character actually knows.
